### dkmobilewash/prova — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 30/30
- URL: https://github.com/dkmobilewash/prova
- Exact inspected revision: `f969900ed3527ce580a5fe986e0f3ecc6e0e8de4` (supporting inspected commits include `87c569a05eef2b56303c1f1303dc7f073e8f8ff7`, `020a4f5c54ce76106e129ad6b4d1c190a4685002`, `4bb697621ef15a659b7818e5c71ffe86e767f943`, `7f4f365758805186000cd8456380cf8323deceda`).
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: unusually deep commercial-subcontractor operating system spanning pending/executed change orders, line-item/contract-sum mutation, T&M tickets with on-site signature, unbilled change orders, daily field-delay reports, submittals/RFIs, pay-app status/disputes, retainage/closeout, backcharge exposure, outbound delivery events, warranty, labor/fringe/compliance, DocuSign evidence and contract-document versioning. The change-order logic distinguishes requested PCO value from executed contract value, refuses proposals against scope already removed, reports unbookable exposure instead of silently pricing it, blocks reopening an older approved CO when a later approved CO touched the same scope, and carries removed scope into pay-app math at earned-to-date rather than inventing/erasing contract value.
- Buyer/problem: commercial specialty subcontractors and self-perform contractors lose money when T&M proof, delay records, PCOs, delivery evidence, backcharge objection windows, pay-app disputes, retainage and signed contract records live in separate systems or are commercially mis-stated.
- Likely first paid wedge: fixed-fee recovery audit that imports active-job commercial records and produces unbilled COs, unresponded backcharges, pending-vs-executed exposure, missing proof, closeout/retainage blockers and notice-delivery exceptions.
- Monetization: recovery/audit service, then recurring subcontractor commercial-controls SaaS; implementation/data migration and managed project-controls layer.
- Build-time/domain advantage: exceptional; compresses many months of real subcontractor domain modeling, money-state edge cases, evidence semantics and test discovery.
- Evidence inspected: current repository/root contents; commit `87c569...` documents 3,000+ tests and rules for latest-revision submittals, backcharge exposure, daily reports as contemporaneous claim evidence, captured-at photo dates, pay-app status, outbound SENT vs DELIVERED vs BOUNCED semantics, T&M ticket gap, unbilled CO read tool and closeout/retainage logic; commit `020a4f...` contains tested change-order bookability/reopen-conflict rules and exact-money regressions; `4bb697...` fixes pay-app treatment of scope removed by CO; `7f4f365...` stores completed DocuSign copies/certificates as executed contract versions.
- Actual public license / rights: no root `LICENSE` appeared in the inspected repository-root listing. User's standing assertion of separate commercial permission is the working authorization for repository-owned code/content. External DocuSign/provider APIs, third-party packages, customer data and other independently owned assets remain separately governed.
- Score: A5 / B5 / C5 / D5 / E5 / F5 = 30/30. Fast recovery wedge, high ACV ceiling, extreme domain compression, unusually rare money/evidence state, extensive mutation/regression evidence, and separate commercial permission asserted by user.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal revision/quantity finding -> cited entitlement/notice deadline -> Prova daily/T&M/photo/delivery proof -> pending CO/unbilled exposure -> pay app/retainage/backcharge outcome. This directly fills several current P0 gaps: trigger/field evidence, delivery state, cost/labor proof, reviewer/commercial state and realized billing outcome.
- Next action: benchmark one held-out real-authorized change from field event through T&M/daily proof, PCO submission, delivery status, approval/rejection, contract-sum mutation and pay-app result; map each state to the existing ScopeSignal evidence IDs.

### MakingMofongo/co-ver-change-order-demo — STRONG / MASTER REFERRAL — 29/30
- URL: https://github.com/MakingMofongo/co-ver-change-order-demo
- Exact inspected revision: `5b5df169c42470f245db1c736ca00a3159ff06dd`
- Date inspected: 2026-09-19
- Category: Repository / Reusable Component / Business Opportunity
- Concrete capability: deterministic owner-side change-order audit engine. It extracts CO line items/units/prices/scope/markups, compares them to original-contract unit prices and allowed terms, flags math errors, duplicates, above-contract unit rates, scope creep/no-baseline conditions and excessive O&P, reconciles totals and exposes estimator approve/dispute review. Potential exposure is computed deterministically; duplicate flags are de-duplicated so the same billed line is not double-counted. Optional AI is extraction/supporting UX rather than the money authority.
- Buyer/problem: owners, owner's reps, CMs and GCs need a defensible pre-pay review of contractor/subcontractor COs; manual spreadsheet review misses duplicate lines, contract-rate drift, unsupported markup and scope leakage.
- Likely first paid wedge: fixed-fee audit of a batch of pending COs against the customer's signed contract schedule/rate/markup terms, with an estimator-reviewed exposure report.
- Monetization: per-CO audit, managed commercial review, recurring owner/CM pre-pay SaaS.
- Build-time/domain advantage: high; provides tested deterministic commercial-review rules, sample scenarios and human dispute/approval workflow that would otherwise take months of claims/cost-control discovery.
- Evidence inspected: `README.md`; `src/lib/engine/analyze.ts`; `src/lib/engine/analyze.test.ts`; tree containing verify pipeline, estimator review/dispute UI and generated sample PDFs. Tests cover tolerance boundaries, exact exposure, duplicate handling, scope-creep vs no-baseline distinction, excessive O&P, rollup reconciliation and multiple sample cases.
- Actual public license / rights: no root `LICENSE` was found at this exact revision. User's standing separate commercial permission is assumed for repository-owned code/content; bundled third-party libraries/assets remain separately governed.
- Score: A5 / B5 / C5 / D4 / E5 / F5 = 29/30. Direct-money wedge and unusually strong tested rules; rarity is slightly below Prova because CO auditing is a known category, though this implementation is undernoticed.
- Combination opportunities: ScopeSignal detected change + OpenTakeoff quantity delta + contract/spec authority -> co-ver rate/markup/duplicate/scope audit -> human reviewer -> BuildSuite/Prova approved commercial state. This creates both contractor recovery and owner-side leakage-control products from the same evidence graph.
- Next action: replace demo baseline terms with amendment/supersession/flow-down-aware cited contract authority and run a held-out authorized CO packet end-to-end.

### Run synthesis
- Highest-value new component: `dkmobilewash/prova` because it closes multiple money/evidence gaps simultaneously: contemporaneous field proof, signed T&M, pending/executed CO state, unbilled COs, backcharge response windows, notice-delivery state, pay-app/retainage/closeout and executed-contract evidence.
- Highest-value adjacent business: `MakingMofongo/co-ver-change-order-demo` creates an owner-side contract-leakage/audit product from the same evidence graph that ScopeSignal uses for contractor recovery.
- Highest-value trigger-lineage engine: `tahseen137/construction-change-order-permit-os` proves permit blocker/owner request -> ChangeEvent -> RFQ/quote -> approval -> exportable CO package.
- Recommended held-out benchmark: revision/field trigger -> quantity/scope evidence -> contract authority/notice deadline -> T&M/daily/photo/delivery proof -> priced PCO -> owner-side co-ver audit -> human approval/rejection -> executed contract sum -> pay-app/retainage outcome. Preserve the same evidence/change identity across every state.
